title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls and add utilization reporting v2
author: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: Implements more conservative burst token accounting in the Dedicated fleet autoscaler, adds a new per-fleet utilization reporting pipeline (v2) that surfaces headroom and burst consumption, and ships a migration for existing burst configs. Motivation: Customers running Dedicated reported tail latency spikes during coordinated burst usage and lacked visibility into cross-tenant burst consumption. This PR 1) fixes an under-accounting bug where in-flight prefetched tokens were not deducted from available burst budget, 2) introduces burst decay windows and soft caps to reduce oscillation, 3) emits a new utilization report (daily and hourly) that shows sustained throughput, burst spend, and effective headroom per fleet, and 4) migrates legacy burst_policy entries to the new schema with validation and rollback hooks. Changes are backwards-compatible except for a documented burst config field rename (burst_rate -> burst_tokens_per_min) that is auto-migrated. Checklist: - [x] Autoscaler accounting change implemented and unit-tested - [x] Utilization reporting pipeline implemented and tested end-to-end on staging - [x] Migration tool included with dry-run mode - [x] Console dashboards updated to surface new metrics - [x] Docs and changelog entries added Rollout plan: 1) Deploy autoscaler accounting and reporting in staging for 48h, validate SLOs and report consistency 2) Enable migration in dry-run on production for 72h, verify no config drift 3) Flip migration and enable new reporting flags for 5% of fleets for 24h, monitor latency and incident metrics 4) Gradual rollout to all fleets over 7 days with rollback on >1% error or >10% tail latency regression Compatibility and failure modes: - Autoscaler will fall back to previous accounting if the migration fails; fallback path exercised in unit tests - Reporting pipeline writes to a new table namespace; reads fall back to raw metrics for older dashboards - Migration validates schema and will abort if unknown fields present Testing: unit tests for accounting edge cases, integration test bench simulating burst load, canary on two low-traffic fleets, manual verification of reporting outputs on staging Metrics to watch post-rollout: P90/P99 inference latency, per-fleet burst consumption, scaling events per-minute, reported headroom. References: ENG-3421 (autoscaling stability), PM-198 (customer ask: predictable burst SLAs). Related PRs: pr-21437-dedicated-autoscaling-burst-controls.json (prior work), pr-178901-dedicated-autoscale-burst-utilization-reporting.json (util reporting initial version).
